newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Akcansa says 96 tables not to international standard.
newsitem.headline: Turk Akcansa says 96 tables not to international standard.

text.p: Turkish cement company Akcansa A.S. said its 1996 financial tables were not prepared according to international standards and therefore could not be used to estimate the per share profits of its foreign partner Belgian cement maker CBR.

In a statement on Thursday, Akcansa said its financial reports were prepared according to Turkish capital market laws and not according to international accounting standards and inflation accounting rules.
"For this reason, our accounts can in no way be used or interpreted to forecast their effects on the per share profit estimates of CBR or Heidelberger Zement," it said.
CBR is a unit of German Heidelberger Zement.

Early last year, CBR took a 97.7 percent share in Turkey's Canakkale Cimento. Half of the stake was swapped a few months later for a 30 percent share in another Turkish cement company Akcimento, owned by Turkish Sabanci conglomerate.
As of October 1, the merged entity was renamed Akcansa, with 79.4 percent owned in equal parts by CBR and Sabanci groups.
Akcansa reported a net profit of 639.63 billion lira in 1996, up from Canakkale Cimento and Akcimento's total profits of 318.5 billion in 1995.
